doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Algiers places, ball games and Frankie Duson
title: Frankie Duson's rivalry with Buddy Johnson, home and parents
summary: Russell asks about Duson's rivalry with Buddy Johnson, where he lived and his family. Tom and Martin say they played together, that he grew up in McDonoghville, that his father, a barber, looked somewhat Mexican, and that he was an only child.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah, I guess try them all. Is there anything else you can tell about Frankie Dooson? Where did he live? Where was his house about? Where did he hang out? Nah. Did he get along all right with Buddy Johnson? Were they rivals?
Yeah, they did. They played together.
Played together. I didn't know whether they were sort of rivals.

What made him, it wasn't Buddy. According to Eddie who took his job, it was the other fellow, the leader. Yeah. Then he come over here and took Connie's job. Yeah. With the dog's lawn. Yeah. Took Connie's job with, what you call it, Buddy Bowler.

Yeah. Did Frankie Dooson live over there most of his life? I think he's buried over there, somebody told me. I don't know where he was. In McDonaldville. I think he's. Yeah, he raised, born and raised over there.
Born and raised over there. Born and raised over there. Yeah. His father was a kind of a Mexican like. Old man Dooson. Old man Dooson, but he was a barber.
Yeah.
And his father, he favors his father.
Yeah.
Yeah.
I saw a picture of Frankie Dooson. Not a very good picture, but I didn't see one or two pictures of him.
Yeah. With the old man or the young one?
No, the young one.
Oh, yeah.
Was the old man named Frankie too? Was maybe?
I don't know. No. But it was Dooson, that's all I know. Yeah.
He used to call him old man Dooson. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
Frankie didn't have any brothers or anyone that played music, I guess. No.
I mean, that's the only one they had. That's the only one I know. The only child they had. Yeah. And it was sports, you know, he didn't work, he didn't do nothing but play music.
He was pretty good. Tall, slim, brown-skinned dude with slick hair. Yeah.
Yeah. Well, his father was kind of a Mexican. Yeah.
